WHEREAS, the Cook County Health and Hospital System (CCHHS) is the largest provider of healthcare services in Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners, in recommending and approving the annual appropriation bill, has invested in many programs to protect the health and well-being of persons in Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, on June 1, 2010, the Cook County Board of Commissioners voted to make permanent the independent Board of Directors overseeing the Cook County Health and Hospitals System; and 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners retains oversight authority over the hospital system through passage of the budget for CCHHS, as well as appointment authority over directors appointed to the Board of Directors.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners does hereby request that a meeting of the Health and Hospitals Committee be convened to discuss the operations of the Cook County Health and Hospital System. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the senior staff of the Cook County Health and Hospital System appear before the Committee and be prepared to update the Committee on the CCHHS’s services and operations.

il-17031-bos-matter-80854.title:
PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDMENT
VITAL RECORDS FEES FOR COUNTY CLERK

BE IT ORDAINED, by the Cook County Board of Commissioners, that CHAPTER 2 ADMINISTRATION, ARTICLE IV OFFICERS AND EMPLOYEES, Subdivision II. Fees, Section 2-174 Vital records fees for County Clerk is hereby amended as follows: 

Sec. 2-174. Vital records fees for County Clerk.
(a)	Birth records. The Cook County Clerk shall continue to charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a birth record as set out in Section 32-1. The following individuals may receive a copy of their birth record at no cost. 
(1)	Individuals, or not for profit organizations representing such individuals, who meet the definition of homeless as defined by Section 103 the federal McKinney-Vento Homeless Assistance Act of 1987, (42 U.S.C. 11302, et seq.), or any individual residing in any of the living situations defined in 42 U.S.C. 11434a(2), as such statutes existed at the time of the enactment of this ordinance; or 
(2)	Individuals in the custody of, or who have been released within the previous 90 days by, the Cook County Department of Corrections or the Illinois Department of Corrections; or 
(3) Individuals who are the victims of domestic, sexual, or gender violence, and their dependents, and who provide documentation from the entity where the individual has sought assistance in addressing domestic violence, sexual violence, or gender violence. The documentation may come from an employee, agent or volunteer of any victim services organization, such as a shelter or non-profit organization, an attorney or legal aid organization, a member of the clergy, or a medical provider. Documentation may also include an official police report or court order. Documents must be dated within the last 12 months. 

The Cook County Clerk may promulgate regulations to determine how individuals can apply for a no cost birth record. 
(b)	Marriage records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a marriage license, sealing, filing and recording the same and the certificate thereunto as set out in Section 32-1. The Cook County Clerk shall continue to charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a marriage record as set out in Section 32-1. 
(c)	Death records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a death record as set out in Section 32-1. 
(d)	Genealogical records. The County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee as set out in Section 32-1 for the first copy and a fee as set out in Section 32-1 for subsequent copies of any genealogical birth, death or marriage certificate. 
(e)	Emergency fee. The County Clerk shall charge and collect an emergency fee as set out in Section 32-1 for providing a copy of a vital record on an overnight basis. The emergency fee authorized in this subsection shall be in addition to any other fees authorized to be collected by the County Clerk for providing the requested document. 
(f)	Waiver and refund of death record fee. The County Clerk shall waive the County portion of the vital records fee for death records requested (first copy only) as set forth in Section 32-1 by those persons legally authorized to request and obtain a death certificate and seeking a copy of a death certificate for a decedent buried at Burr Oak Cemetery. Said waiver shall apply only to death records indicating a date of death prior to July 6, 2009, and burial at Burr Oak Cemetery; the waiver extends only to the County's portion of the fee for the first copy only and shall not extend to requests for additional copies. The County Clerk is required to continue to collect a $2.00 fee for the first copy of the death record as required by State Statute unless waived by the State. The waiver shall run through September 15, 2009, unless otherwise authorized by the Cook County Board of Commissioners. In accordance with the County Clerk's records, the County Clerk is hereby authorized to refund Cook County's portion of the death records fee for death records requested (first copy only) to those individuals who legally requested and obtained a death record/certificate since July 6, 2009, for a decedent buried at Burr Oak Cemetery. 
(g)	Civil Union records. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a civil union license, sealing, filing and recording the same and the certificate thereunto as set out in Section 32-1. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the first copy, and a fee for each additional copy of a civil union record as set out in Section 32-1. 
(h)	Commemorative Certificates. The Cook County Clerk shall charge and collect a fee for the issuance of a Commemorative Certificate of Marriage or for the issuance of a Commemorative Certificate of Civil Union as set out in Section 32-1. With each Commemorative Certificate issued, the Clerk shall also issue a certified copy of the underlying record. The fee charged and collected as set forth in Section 32-1 shall cover the cost of both the commemorative certificate and the certified copy. 
Effective Date: This ordinance shall be in effect on February 01, 2027

il-17031-bos-matter-81288.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

COOK COUNTY COMMUNITY VIOLENCE INTERVENTION INITIATIVE FALL 2026 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Justice Advisory Council (JAC), as an office under the Cook County Board President, works to promote equitable, human-centered, community-driven justice system innovation and practice through rigorous stakeholder engagement, policy work, service coordination, and grantmaking that increases community safety and reduces reliance on incarceration; and   

WHEREAS, the JAC supports Cook County’s commitment to advancing equity throughout Cook County by administering grants that invest in programs and strategies to improve community safety in areas of violence prevention and reentry; and  
  
WHEREAS, Cook County Ordinance Sec. 2-527 establishes the JAC’s authority to administer violence prevention, intervention and reduction grants to nonprofit community-based organizations in accordance with the Cook County Procurement Code; and 

WHEREAS, building on historic levels of investment in community-based organizations, JAC grant initiatives will sustain key services beyond American Rescue Plan Act funding, supporting organizations that help those closest to the gun violence epidemic to access critical programs and services that contribute to increased community safety throughout Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, gun violence dramatically affects physical, cognitive, mental, emotional wellbeing and development of those exposed to it: direct survivors of gun violence and the communities impacted by incidences of gun violence; and  

WHEREAS direct and indirect survivors are at greater risk of perpetrating violence, experiencing further victimization or exposure to violence; and 
 
WHEREAS our communities are less safe when those at risk of perpetrating or being impacted by gun violence cannot access critical services essential to violence prevention; and 
 
WHEREAS, in 2025 the JAC launched Cook County Community Violence Intervention (CC-CVI) and Cook County Wraparound Services for Survivors of Gun Violence (CC-SGV), complementary grant initiatives designed to improve community safety in Cook County; and
  
WHEREAS, the CC-CVI initiative provides services to residents at risk of being involved in gun violence; and  

WHEREAS, funding for the CC-CVI initiative is working in partnership with the Government Alliance for Safe Communities (GASC) in alignment with the philanthropic and business communities and our collaborative investment strategy to maximize the impact of state and local funding for violence prevention; and
  
WHEREAS, the GASC strategy and CC-CVI initiative represent a comprehensive approach to violence prevention, utilizing innovative, emerging programming and services, supported by evidence-based research from institutions such as Northwestern University’s Center for Neighborhood Engaged Research & Science (CORNERS), to engage individuals at the highest risk of firearm violence (HRI’s); and
  
WHEREAS, Chicago saw the lowest rates of gun homicides in 2025, with that trend continuing in 2026, notably following these historic levels of investment in community-based approaches to violence prevention; and 
 
WHEREAS, the CC-CVI initiative funds community organizations to provide services in each of the following categories: 
·	Street Outreach: Street outreach workers mediate conflicts and prevent retaliatory violence between those who are at risk of being involved in gun violence. Street outreach workers engage with individuals at highest risk of violence in a variety of settings, including parks, homes, street corners, community centers, schools, and hospitals at all hours of the day.   
·	Case Management: Case management includes developing case plans based on individuals’ unique needs and providing or connecting individuals to identified resources and services. Services can be provided directly or through linkages with other providers and include but are not limited to: effective emotional or trauma related therapies, legal aid services, housing services, employment training, job placement services, family engagement, and other support services.   
·	Victim Services: Victim service advocates help families and victims of violence recover from physical and emotional trauma by empowering them with skills, services, and opportunities; and 

WHEREAS, funding for the CC-CVI initiative is strategically targeted to provide services in the geographic areas defined as communities impacted by gun violence in the Reimagine Public Safety Act (RPSA) (430 ILCS 69); and 

WHEREAS, the RPSA calls for a comprehensive approach to reducing firearm violence through targeted, integrated behavioral health services; and  
 
WHEREAS, the JAC released the first notice of funding opportunity for the CC-CVI initiative in March 2025 and the Cook County Board of Commissioners authorized awards for 18 organizations in July 2025 via resolution #25-0704; and 
 
WHEREAS, the awards proposed herein are pursuant to the second notice of funding opportunity for the CC-CVI initiative released in July 2026; and 
 
WHEREAS, this funding opportunity was strategically designed in support of two key goals of the GASC: targeting services to HRI’s and to serve at least 25% of HRI’s in RPSA areas across all of Cook County; and 
  
WHEREAS, this funding opportunity included two potential funding tracks; and 
 
WHEREAS, funding Track 1 is for a coalition of organizations under one lead entity to serve HRI’s in RPSA areas in the City of Chicago; and   
 
WHEREAS, Track 2 awards are for organizations that will serve HRI’s in RPSA areas across Cook County in which the goal of reaching 25% of HRI’s, across GASC investments, has not yet been met; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners authorized the allocation of $20 million in Equity Funds in the FY2026 budget for the Justice Advisory Council to support community violence intervention; and   
 
WHEREAS, $5 million of those funds were awarded via resolution 26-0721 in July 2026 to nine organizations pursuant to the first funding opportunity; and 
 
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED, the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby authorizes the Justice Advisory Council to issue 2-year agreements with the following organizations: 
1. Alliance of Local Service Organizations in an aggregate amount up to $1,485,000.00, serving Humboldt Park.

il-17031-bos-matter-81391.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING A VACANT LAND PROPERTY TAX INCENTIVE FOR VACANT PROPERTY ACQUIRED IN COOK COUNTY 

WHEREAS, Cook County is a home rule unit of local government pursuant to Article VII, Section 6 of the Illinois Constitution; and 

WHEREAS, Cook County currently provides property tax incentives, including Class 7b, to encourage investment, redevelopment, rehabilitation, and productive reuse of property; and 

WHEREAS, Class 7b provides qualifying commercial properties with a reduced assessment level of 10 percent for ten years, 15 percent in the eleventh year, and 20 percent in the twelfth year; and 

WHEREAS, existing property tax incentives are primarily structured around buildings and development projects and do not adequately address the distinct challenges associated with vacant land that must first be acquired, assembled, remediated, planned, and prepared for productive reuse; and 

WHEREAS, the Cook County Land Bank Authority ("CCLBA"), developers, community organizations, and other property owners acquire vacant, abandoned, and distressed properties and can facilitate their return to productive use; and 

WHEREAS, strategic acquisition and assembly of vacant parcels can support affordable housing, homeownership, community ownership, community land trusts, economic development, parks, open space, urban agriculture, environmental remediation, cultural uses, and other neighborhood assets; and 

WHEREAS, the assembly of multiple parcels may require substantial time for acquisition, title clearance, environmental assessment and remediation, zoning, surveying, infrastructure coordination, utilities, curb cuts, easements, community planning, financing, and identification of qualified development or community ownership partners; and 

WHEREAS, a temporary property tax incentive during this land assembly period would reduce the carrying costs associated with vacant land and facilitate coordinated, neighborhood-scale acquisition and redevelopment; and 

WHEREAS, such an incentive would support a "buy back the block" approach in which any party acquiring vacant land in Cook County can strategically acquire and assemble contiguous or strategically related parcels rather than relying solely upon parcel-by-parcel disposition; and 

WHEREAS, the incentive should encourage productive land assembly while preventing indefinite or speculative holding of vacant property; and 

WHEREAS, a twelve-month initial assembly period, with the possibility of two additional one-year extensions based upon documented progress, provides a defined framework for complex land assembly while maintaining accountability; and

WHEREAS, Section 9-150 of the Illinois Property Tax Code, 35 ILCS 200/9-150, provides that a property classification for purposes of taxation must be established by ordinance of the County Board.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of Cook County, assembled this 19th day of November, 2026, that Cook County hereby establishes as County policy the creation of a Vacant Land Property Tax Incentive for qualifying vacant real property acquired by any person or entity in Cook County. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Cook County Bureau of Economic Development, in consultation with the CCLBA, Cook County Assessor, Cook County Treasurer, Cook County Clerk, Cook County Department of Planning and Development, Bureau of Finance, and State's Attorney's Office, shall develop and present an implementing ordinance establishing a legally permissible property tax classification or incentive for qualifying vacant land acquired in Cook County. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the proposed incentive shall, where legally permissible, provide qualifying property with a full exemption from and abatement of property taxes during the assembly period. All benefits of the incentive shall end when the assembly period ends, at which time the property shall be assessed at the level otherwise applicable under law and the owner shall be responsible for all resulting property taxes. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That eligible property shall include vacant land located anywhere in Cook County and acquired after the adoption date of this Resolution by any person or entity through purchase, donation, tax-delinquency proceedings, governmental transfer, deed in lieu of foreclosure, land-banking agreement, or other lawful acquisition mechanism, whether from the CCLBA, a private seller, or another source. Land acquired on or before the adoption date shall not qualify. Eligible land must have been vacant for 36 or more consecutive months. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That qualifying property may consist of one or more parcels acquired as part of an approved land assembly, neighborhood stabilization, development, community ownership, affordable housing, environmental, open-space, agricultural, cultural, recreational, or other productive-use strategy. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the proposed incentive shall provide an initial twelve (12) month land assembly period during which qualifying vacant property may receive the incentive while the owner completes parcel assembly, environmental remediation, zoning, infrastructure coordination, community planning, financing, development planning, or preparation for community ownership or productive reuse. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Bureau of Economic Development may approve up to two (2) additional one-year extensions of the assembly period when additional time is necessary to complete an approved land assembly, remediation, development, community ownership, or disposition strategy.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the maximum assembly period shall be thirty-six (36) months, consisting of the initial twelve-month period and up to two twelve-month extensions, and that each extension shall require documented progress and an approved work plan identifying remaining milestones and the anticipated productive use, development, disposition, or community ownership of the property. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That continued eligibility shall be conditioned upon demonstrated progress toward productive reuse and shall not be available for indefinite or speculative holding of vacant land. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the program shall prioritize land assembly and projects that advance: 

1. Affordable housing and homeownership; 
2. Community ownership and community land trusts; 
3. Neighborhood stabilization; 
4. Strategic assembly of contiguous or strategically related parcels; 
5. Parks, open space, greenways, and community gardens; 
6. Urban agriculture and food production; 
7. Environmental assessment and remediation; 
8. Cultural, artistic, recreational, and community uses; 
9. Neighborhood-serving commercial and economic development; and 
10. Other community-supported productive uses. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That, where legally permissible, multiple parcels acquired as part of a coordinated land assembly shall be eligible to participate collectively in the incentive, including parcels intended to be consolidated or transferred under common ownership or control. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That upon completion of the assembly period, property proceeding into an eligible development or permanent productive use may transition to another property tax classification or incentive for which it independently qualifies under applicable law. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the implementing ordinance shall establish transparent eligibility, application, certification, extension, reporting, monitoring, suspension, termination, and enforcement requirements and shall include appropriate safeguards against speculative or indefinite land holding. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Bureau of Economic Development, in consultation with the CCLBA, shall report annually to the Cook County Board regarding properties participating in the program, parcels assembled, extensions granted, productive uses achieved, community ownership outcomes, and the fiscal impact of the incentive.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the implementing ordinance shall be presented to the Cook County Board of Commissioners within 180 days of adoption of this Resolution. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That nothing in this Resolution shall be construed to supersede the authority or statutory duties of the Cook County Assessor, Treasurer, Clerk, municipalities, or other taxing bodies, and implementation shall be subject to applicable Illinois law. 

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, That the Clerk of the Cook County Board of Commissioners is hereby authorized and directed to transmit certified copies of this Resolution to the Cook County Assessor, Cook County Treasurer, Cook County Bureau of Economic Development, Cook County Department of Planning and Development, Cook County Land Bank Authority, and Cook County State's Attorney's Office. 

Effective Date: This Resolution shall be in full force and effect immediately upon its adoption.

il-17031-bos-matter-81439.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

PROPOSED RESOLUTION TO ADDRESS LABOR AND DELIVERY UNIT CLOSURES AND PROMOTE COLLABORATIVE STATE AND COUNTY-WIDE ACTION TO PROTECT MATERNAL HEALTHCARE IN CHICAGO’S SOUTH SIDE AND SOUTH SUBURBAN UNDERSERVED COMMUNITIES

WHEREAS, access to safe, timely, and affordable maternal healthcare is essential to protecting the lives of pregnant individuals, mothers, and newborns throughout Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Department of Public Health’s 2025 Maternal Mortality Data Report found that during 2021-2022, pregnancy-related mortality was 78 deaths per 100,000 live births among Black women, compared with 33 among White women; and 42 per 100,000 among Chicago residents, compared with 32 among suburban Cook County residents; and

WHEREAS, 91% of pregnancy-related deaths reviewed in Illinois during 2021-2022 were determined to be potentially preventable, underscoring the importance of timely medical care, accessible maternity services, and coordinated preventive interventions; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Department of Public Health’s Blueprint for Birth Equity reports that Illinois experienced a 27% net reduction in birthing facilities between 2016 and 2023, with 32 obstetric hospitals closing; and Chicago’s South Side, where majority-Black neighborhoods are served by only three of the city’s 16 birthing hospitals, has been particularly affected; and more than one-third of Illinois counties are classified as maternity care deserts; and

WHEREAS, the loss of labor-and-delivery units can increase travel distances, delay emergency obstetric care, disrupt prenatal and postpartum continuity, strain neighboring hospitals, threaten healthcare employment, and disproportionately burden low-income families and historically underserved communities; and

WHEREAS, Roseland Community Hospital has announced plans to discontinue labor-and-delivery services effective October 31, 2026, citing financial pressures, further reducing maternity-care options for Chicago’s Far South Side and surrounding south suburban communities; and

WHEREAS, Cook County has previously considered maternal healthcare through Resolution 25-0917 and adopted Resolution 25-2301 declaring maternal morbidity and mortality a public health crisis; and Illinois has established the Blueprint for Birth Equity and existing hospital reimbursement and financial-support initiatives, demonstrating the importance of coordinated implementation and timely intervention; and

WHEREAS, Illinois House Bill 3453, introduced in the 104th General Assembly, proposed at least 120 days’ public notice and a public meeting before a hospital discontinued a perinatal unit, but was re-referred to the House Rules Committee on March 21, 2025; and

WHEREAS, state-level officials have expressed support for convening relevant stakeholders to address labor-and-delivery unit closures and advance coordinated action to protect access to maternal healthcare throughout Chicago’s South Side and south suburban underserved communities; and

WHEREAS, additional coordinated action is needed to identify threatened maternity services, assess regional capacity, evaluate available resources, and develop feasible interventions before further closures occur, without duplicating existing initiatives.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, Cook County Commissioner Dr. Kisha, E. McCaskill, and the Cook County Board of Commissioners, calls to convene a public hearing to address labor-and-delivery unit closures and suggest governmental action to protect maternal healthcare access, with particular attention to the underserved communities on Chicago’s South Side and in the south suburbs; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the hearing shall use the existing studies to identify the implementation of safeguards to directly address the maternity-unit closures; regional hospital capacity; maternal and newborn safety; transportation and continuity-of-care barriers; workforce and community impacts; and existing (allocated/allotted) government funding and grants, reimbursement, and other resources available to stabilize, sustain and/or coordinate safe alternative care; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that appropriate governing agencies, hospitals, municipalities, healthcare professionals, and community organizations are encouraged to collaborate to identify threatened services, assess available resources and barriers, and pursue feasible interventions, and recommend specific next steps for early intervention and coordinated action; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners would encourage impacted hospital(s) such as Roseland to establishing a temporary moratorium on labor-and-delivery unit closures until appropriate community-impact assessments, public engagement, and safe transition plans are completed, reviewed and accepted by the respective governing bodies, and shared with the community and other stakeholders, with appropriate exceptions to protect immediate patient safety; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a request shall be made to the Cook County Clerk to transmit copies of this resolution to the respective governing agencies and partners for their consideration and appropriate action.

il-17031-bos-matter-81458.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

REQUESTING THE COOK COUNTY BOARD’S CRIMINAL JUSTICE COMMITTEE TO CONVENE A HEARING REGARDING THE RESPECTIVE AUTHORITY, RESPONSIBILITIES, AND INVESTIGATIVE OVERSIGHT PROCEDURES OF THE COOK COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE AND THE OFFICE OF THE INDEPENDENT INSPECTOR GENERAL

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the importance of transparency, accountability, fairness, and public confidence in the administration of County government and its public safety institutions; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Sheriff’s Office is an independently elected office responsible for carrying out significant law enforcement, correctional, and public safety responsibilities under Illinois law; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Office of the Independent Inspector General (OIIG) is established under County ordinance to promote integrity, accountability, and responsible government through the exercise of its legally authorized oversight and investigative functions; and

WHEREAS, both the Sheriff’s Office and the OIIG perform important public functions, and clarity regarding their respective legal authority, responsibilities, and procedures is essential to effective government operations; and

WHEREAS, questions have arisen concerning the scope of the OIIG’s authority to review certain investigations involving Sheriff’s Office personnel and the respective responsibilities of both offices in addressing allegations of misconduct; and

WHEREAS, the OIIG has identified and communicated recommendations concerning investigative procedures, including:

The identification, documentation, and appropriate consideration of allegations arising from complaints, video recordings, reports, and other available evidence;

The establishment and consistent application of procedures for informational complaints and external referrals, including appropriate management notification, documentation, and disposition;

The application of consistent investigative standards, including witness interviews, examination of relevant evidence, identification of potential subjects, and documentation of investigative findings and decisions; and

WHEREAS, differences in interpretation or implementation of these recommendations warrant further examination to better understand the legal, operational, and administrative considerations of the respective offices; and

WHEREAS, concerns have also been raised regarding the handling and disposition of certain complaints involving Sheriff’s Office personnel, including a reported incident involving allegations that an employee reported for duty while impaired and possessed an allegedly unlawful firearm; and

WHEREAS, the inclusion of such allegations in this Resolution is solely for the purpose of identifying matters appropriate for procedural review and shall not be construed as a determination that misconduct occurred or that any investigation was improperly conducted; and

WHEREAS, the OIIG has established a Public Safety Oversight Unit to address matters within its asserted oversight responsibilities, and questions concerning the unit’s legal authority, operational scope, coordination, and relationship with existing investigative functions warrant examination; and

WHEREAS, the OIIG has requested that the Cook County Board’s Criminal Justice Committee convene a public hearing to examine these matters; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board’s Criminal Justice Committee has an interest in ensuring that County public safety institutions operate within their respective legal authority and maintain appropriate standards of transparency, accountability, due process, and public trust; and

WHEREAS, a hearing would provide an appropriate forum for the Sheriff’s Office, the OIIG, and other relevant parties to present their respective positions, explain existing procedures, and identify opportunities for improved coordination and clarity; and

WHEREAS, the purpose of such a hearing is to gather information, clarify applicable legal and administrative responsibilities, and evaluate existing policies and procedures without prejudging the conduct, legal position, or conclusions of any individual or office.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners requests that the Criminal Justice Committee convene a hearing for the following purposes:

1.	Legal Authority and Jurisdiction: Examine the respective legal authority, jurisdiction, and responsibilities of the Cook County Sheriff’s Office and the OIIG under applicable Illinois law and Cook County ordinances.

2.	Investigative Standards and Procedures: Review the policies, procedures, and standards used to receive, investigate, document, refer, and resolve complaints involving Sheriff’s Office personnel.

3.	 Recommendations and Responses: Examine the OIIG’s investigative recommendations and the Sheriff’s Office’s responses, including any legal, operational, or administrative considerations influencing their implementation.

4.	Complaint Review and Disposition: Review the procedures followed in selected matters involving allegations of employee misconduct, including the reported impaired-and-armed employee incident, to determine whether existing policies provide appropriate standards of documentation, review, accountability, and due process.

5.	Public Safety Oversight Unit: Examine the purpose, legal authority, responsibilities, and operational scope of the OIIG’s Public Safety Oversight Unit, including its relationship with existing Sheriff’s Office investigative and accountability functions.

6.	Interagency Coordination: Identify opportunities to strengthen communication, coordination, and the appropriate exchange of information between the Sheriff’s Office and the OIIG while respecting their respective legal responsibilities.

7.	Potential Improvements: Consider whether additional policy guidance, administrative procedures, interagency agreements, or legislative clarification may be appropriate to strengthen transparency, accountability, and public confidence.

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Criminal Justice Committee shall conduct the hearing in an impartial manner, affording the Sheriff’s Office, the OIIG, and other invited participants a fair and reasonable opportunity to present information, respond to questions, and explain their respective positions; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Committee shall invite testimony from the Cook County Sheriff, the Independent Inspector General, appropriate representatives of their respective offices, relevant legal and administrative experts, and other individuals whose participation may assist the Committee in fulfilling its oversight responsibilities; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Committee shall conduct its proceedings in accordance with applicable law, including requirements concerning confidentiality, personnel privacy, due process, and the protection of ongoing investigations; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that nothing in this Resolution shall be interpreted as a finding of misconduct, an endorsement or rejection of any disputed legal position, or an attempt to interfere with the lawful duties and independent authority of either office; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that following the hearing, the Committee may consider appropriate recommendations concerning legislative clarification, administrative coordination, or improvements to investigative oversight procedures based upon the information presented; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Clerk of the Board shall transmit a copy of this Resolution to the Chair of the Criminal Justice Committee, the Cook County Sheriff, and the Cook County Independent Inspector General.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

A RESOLUTION CONDEMNING THE DEATHLY IMPACT OF USAID CUTS ON GLOBAL HEALTH 

WHEREAS, in 1998, Congress established the United States Agency for International Development (USAID) as a functionally independent executive agency through the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act; and  
 
WHEREAS, under this Act, President Bill Clinton reorganized USAID, which retained its independence from the U.S. Department of State, with its administrator reporting to and being under the direct authority and foreign policy guidance of the Secretary of State; and  
 
WHEREAS, U.S. citizens contribute about 17 cents per day to USAID, around just $64 per year; and  
 
WHEREAS, a study co-authored by a UCLA Fielding School of Public Health found that USAID-supported programs were associated with a 15% reduction in all-cause mortality and a 32% reduction in mortality among children under the age of 5 between 2001 and 2021; and  
 
WHEREAS, in countries receiving high levels of support, mortality from HIV/AIDS was reduced by 74%, malaria by 53%, and other tropical diseases by 51%; and  
 
WHEREAS, the study estimates that more than 91 million deaths were prevented between 2001 and 2021, of which approximately 30 million were children; and 
 
WHEREAS, under President George W. Bush, Congress passed the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act in 2003, creating the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) to address the global HIV/AIDS epidemic and help save the lives of those suffering from the disease; and  
 
WHEREAS, PEPFAR is the largest commitment by any nation to address a single disease in history, enabled by strong bipartisan support across ten U.S. congresses and four presidential administrations; and  
 
WHEREAS, per its authorizing statute, PEPFAR is overseen by a U.S. Global AIDS Coordinator - a Senate-confirmed position appointed by the President and holding the rank of ambassador - at the State Department’s Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy; and  
 
WHEREAS, USAID is PEPFAR’s largest government implementing agency, accounting for roughly 60% of PEPFAR’s bilateral assistance; and  
 
WHEREAS, PEPFAR works closely with partner countries toward achieving HIV/AIDS epidemic control while promoting the long-term sustainability of their responses; and  
 
WHEREAS, since PEPFAR’S inception, the U.S. government has invested over $100 billion in the global HIV/AIDS response, saved 26 million lives, and enabled 7.8 million babies to be born without HIV infection; and   
 
WHEREAS, Studies have also found that PEPFAR funding has been associated with several “spillover” effects including significant reductions in all-cause mortality, increases in childhood immunizations, and increases in GDP growth; and  
 
WHEREAS, PEPFAR has been reauthorized by Congress four times, most recently in March 2024 for just one year; and 
 
WHEREAS, PEPFAR’s authorization was not renewed and expired on March 25, 2025; and 
 
WHEREAS, on March 10, 2025, The Trump administration announced they had officially cancelled 86% of U.S. foreign aid contracts; and  
 
WHEREAS, studies have crucially found that the recent cuts to USAID may lead to more than 14 million additional deaths globally by 2030, including more than 4.5 million children under 5; and 
WHEREAS, an analysis found that of the 770 global health awards identified, 379 included HIV activities, 71% of which were terminated, including several HIV treatment awards as well as most HIV prevention; and  
 
WHEREAS, former civil servant at USAID Nicholas Enrich projected that with these cuts, and assuming they are not restored, an additional one million children will die every year; and  
 
WHEREAS, Enrich also projected that up to 17.9 million more people will contract malaria and as many as 166,000 people will die from it constituting a 39% increase from current rates; and  
 
WHEREAS, additional projections suggest that Tuberculosis cases, including multidrug-resistant TB, will soar by 28 to 32 percent; and  
 
WHEREAS, with these cuts, as many as 28,000 people will suffer from emerging infectious diseases, like Ebola and Marburg; and  
 
WHEREAS, hundreds of millions of people will contract polio infections over the next decade, with an additional 200,000 people becoming paralyzed by polio; and  
 
WHEREAS, Enrich also noted that the cuts could lead to "increasing the likelihood of unchecked outbreaks of emerging infectious diseases such as avian influenza, Ebola, and mpox - threats that can spread globally and endanger American citizens; and  
 
WHEREAS, the sudden withdrawal of U.S. money has caused a systemic shock, with U.N. officials warning that, if the funding isn’t replaced, the cuts could lead to more than 4 million AIDS-related deaths and 6 million more HIV infections by 2029; and  
 
WHEREAS, as a result of these cuts to PEPFAR and USAID, as of July 2026, so far 1,700 global sites providing preventative medicine and treatment have been closed; and  
 
WHEREAS, as of this year, 73 percent of groups that provide services to particularly vulnerable groups, sex workers, men who have sex with men, people who use injection drugs, reported that they have stopped providing at least one type of service; and  
 
WHEREAS, recent reports from 22 neonatal clinics in a network of hospitals in Africa where newborns come to, found that mothers had a 50 percent jump in HIV rates and over 300 percent jump in those places finding women were not on treatment; and  
 
WHEREAS, following these cuts, a tracking survey found that PrEP initiations declined by 13 percent and 66 percent in five high-burden countries between January-September 2024 and January-September 2025 
 
WHEREAS, a recent analysis in 14 countries found that the disruption in PEPFAR funding was associated with significant drops in access from early 2025 through early 2026 and that recovery remains limited, with ongoing reduced access to HIV services and commodities, including antiretroviral treatment, PrEP, HIV tests, and clinical monitoring tests; and  
 
WHEREAS, the ramifications of these cuts to PEPFAR and USAID inevitably trickle down into the lives, communities, and medical systems of residents within Cook County; and  
 
WHEREAS, Cook County continues to advocate for health equity, promoting education and awareness, and supporting organizations that work tirelessly to serve those at risk and living with HIV and AIDS;  
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners does hereby issue its full condemnation of the Trump Administrations’ cuts to USAID and PEPFAR funding, demand the immediate reinstatement of this funding, and mourn the deaths that have and will occur if these cuts are not reversed.

PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDMENT

REQUIRING SEMI-ANNUAL REPORTING ON USE OF AUTOMATIC LICENSE PLATE READERS BY COOK COUNTY SHERIFF’S OFFICE  

BE IT ORDAINED, by the Cook County Board of Commissioners, that Chapter 46, Article II, Division 1, Sec. 46-37.1 of the Cook County Code is hereby amended as Follows: 

Sec 46-37.1. Reporting.

(a)	The Sheriff's Office shall report to the Board of Commissioners quarterly on the cost that the office incurs due to investigating and processing cases involving firearms.

(b)	The Sheriff’s Office shall submit and present a semi-annual report to the Board of Commissioners concerning the use, oversight, and safeguards associated with its Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology. Such reporting shall focus on ALPR systems and contractors, documented investigative use, requests for captured plate data, compliance with State and local law and established policies, auditing procedures, data privacy protections, and measures taken to prevent and address unauthorized use.  The semi-annual reports shall include the following:

(1)	ALPR Systems and Contractors

(a) The total number of ALPRs owned, operated, or otherwise accessed, including the specific number of fixed, mobile and portable devices, and mobile applications;

(b) A complete list of ALPR related contractors, including the contractor services used and length of the contract term for each contractor. 

(c) A complete list of all public, private, and governmental entities that provided the Sheriff’s Office ALPR data and a list of all public, private, and governmental entities that Sheriff’s Office provided ALPR data obtained from systems the Sheriff’s Office directly owns or operates.

(2) Investigative Use and Accountability 

Information concerning the use of ALPR technology for authorized law enforcement purposes, including:

(a)	The total number of license plates searched.

(b)	The number of investigative queries conducted.

(c)	The number of investigations in which ALPR information was documented as having been utilized. 

(3) Requests for captured plate data, including:

(a) The total number of requests received; 

(b) The total number of requests that resulted in the release of CCSO ALPR data and the reason for the request (i.e., reason code);

(c)  The total number of in-state requests, and for each in-state requestor, (i) the specific number of requests that resulted in the release of CCSO ALPR data, (ii) the reason for the request (i.e., ALPR reason code), and (iii) the agency or municipality of the requestor;

(d) The total number of out-of-state requests, and for each out-of-state requestor, (i) the specific number of requests that resulted in a release of CCSO ALPR data, (ii) the reason for the request (i.e., ALPR reason code), and (iii) the agency or municipality and state of the requestor;

(e) The total number of federal requests, and for each federal requestor, (i) the specific number of requests that resulted in a release of CCSO ALPR data, (ii) the reason for the request (i.e., ALPR reason code), and (iii) the associated agency of the requestor;

(4) Auditing and Policy Compliance

Information concerning the Sheriff’s Office’s oversight and auditing of ALPR use, including:

(a)	The number of audits conducted and investigative queries reviewed.

(b)	The scope and methodology of audits conducted during the reporting period.

(c)	The number and list of the types of potential policy violations identified through auditing or other oversight mechanisms.

(d)	Aggregate statistical information regarding the disposition of substantiated violations and any resulting corrective actions, including retraining, suspension, or revocation of system access, or disciplinary referrals, as applicable. If there are multiple substantiated violations attributed to a single user, include the total number of substantiated violation and the corrective action employed for each substantiated violation.

(5) Data Privacy and Access Safeguards

Information concerning the implementation and enforcement of safeguards protecting ALPR information, including:

(a)	Compliance with established data retention and deletion requirements. 

(b)	Enforcement of authorized user access restrictions and authentication requirements.

(c)	Compliance with restrictions governing access to and sharing of ALPR information with all agencies that have executed a Declaration of Investigative Intentions for Access to Cook County Sheriff’s Office ALPR System (“ALPR Declaration”).

(d)	The number of identified incidents involving unauthorized access, use, or disclosure of ALPR information, if any, and the actions taken in response.

(6) Security and Data Protection

Information concerning the security of ALPR information, including:

(a)	Any known identified security incidents or confirmed data breaches involving ALPR information and the source of the security incident or data sharing breach, if known.

(b)	Any substantiated violations of established data-sharing agreements or access restrictions involving all agencies that have executed an ALPR Declaration.

(c)	Actions taken to address identified vulnerabilities, prevent unauthorized access, and strengthen data security protections. 

Limitation of Disclosure of Security and Data Protection Measures. Disclosure under pursuant to this ordinance shall not include information about CCSO’s security system, access controls, or security vulnerabilities, including information relating to any third-party contractor’s software procured by the CCSO, the release of which could reasonably compromise CCSO’s network security, or the network security of a third-party contractor's software, or reveal a third-party contractor's proprietary information otherwise prohibited from disclosure. This Section does not limit disclosures required by CCSO under applicable law.

(7) Safeguards Implementation and Improvements

A summary of any material changes to ALPR policies, procedures, training requirements, access controls, or auditing protocols implemented during the reporting period to strengthen accountability, protect personal information, and ensure compliance with applicable requirements. 

(a)	Reports shall present information and data in aggregate form and shall not require the disclosure of personally identifiable information; confidential investigative information; information that would compromise an active investigation; information that would compromise or interfere with an internal disciplinary process; information that could reasonably compromise network security of CCSO, Cook County, a third-party contractor, or other law enforcement agency; information that could reasonably lead to the disclosure of a third-party contractor’s proprietary information that is otherwise prohibited from disclosure under law or by an agreement between relevant Parties; information relating to another law enforcement agency’s use of its own ALPR system that CCSO is not authorized to release; or information that is otherwise prohibited from disclosure pursuant to State or federal law.

PROPOSED RESOLUTION

PROPOSED RESOLUTION SUPPORTING FULL FEDERAL FUNDING OF THE INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES EDUCATION ACT (IDEA) AND PROMOTING COORDINATED ACTION TO STRENGTHEN SPECIAL EDUCATION SERVICES THROUGHOUT COOK COUNTY

WHEREAS, access to a free public education and equitable educational opportunities for students with disabilities is essential to promoting academic achievement, educational equity, and the long-term success of children and families throughout Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA), originally enacted in 1975, established federal protections and educational requirements for students with disabilities and authorized a federal funding contribution intended to reach 40% of the national average per-pupil expenditure for eligible special education services; and

WHEREAS, despite this longstanding federal funding commitment, the U.S. Department of Education reports that the proposed federal contribution for the current funding year would cover approximately 10% of special education costs nationwide, significantly below the 40% funding benchmark, amounting to a $1.4 billion shortfall for Illinois school districts and

WHEREAS, the number of students receiving services under IDEA has more than doubled over the past five decades, increasing from approximately 3.7 million students in 1976 to a projected 8.3 million students in 2027; and

WHEREAS, school districts throughout Cook County face increasing financial pressures associated with specialized instructional services, qualified educational personnel, transportation, assistive technologies, and other essential resources necessary to meet the educational needs of students with disabilities; and

WHEREAS, continued federal funding shortfalls limit the ability of local school districts to invest in academic enrichment, programming, and other essential services while increasing pressure on local taxpayers; and

WHEREAS, the Illinois Association of School Boards, in partnership with school board associations nationwide, and state partners such as the Illinois Association of School Administrators, the Illinois Principals Association and the Illinois Association of School Business Officials, has launched the 40 by 40: Fulfill the IDEA Promise initiative to advocate for annual increases in federal IDEA appropriations to achieve the 40% funding benchmark by 2040; and

WHEREAS, Cook County recognizes the importance of collaboration among all levels of governments, academic institutions, parents, and community stakeholders in advancing policies that support students with disabilities and strengthen public education; and

WHEREAS, coordinated intergovernmental advocacy, public engagement, and partnerships with educational stakeholders can help elevate the financial challenges facing local school districts, inform policymakers, and advance sustainable federal funding solutions; and

WHEREAS, additional coordinated action is necessary to increase public awareness, identify the impacts of federal special education funding shortfalls on Cook County school districts, and develop a unified regional approach to supporting full federal funding of IDEA;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that Cook County Commissioner Dr. Kisha E. McCaskill and the Cook County Board of Commissioners express their support for the Illinois Association of School Boards' 40 by 40: Fulfill the IDEA Promise initiative calling upon the United States Congress to fulfill its federal funding commitment under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act through sustained annual appropriations increases sufficient to reach the 40% funding benchmark by 2040; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners encourages the convening of community town halls, public forums, and educational discussions throughout Cook County, with particular attention to historically underserved communities, to raise awareness of IDEA funding challenges, provide opportunities for parents, educators, school administrators, and community stakeholders to share their experiences, and identify the impacts of federal funding shortfalls on local educational services; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that Cook County encourages coordinated engagement and Illinois legislators to communicate the challenges of Cook County school districts, support legislation establishing a sustainable pathway toward full IDEA funding; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that information and recommendations developed through community engagement, educational partnerships, and intergovernmental discussions may be shared with appropriate federal and state officials to inform legislative priorities, funding considerations, and future collaborative action; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Clerk is requested to transmit copies of this resolution to the President of the United States, members of the Illinois congressional delegation, the leadership of the United States Senate and House of Representatives, the appropriate congressional appropriations and education committees, the Governor of Illinois, the Illinois General Assembly, the Illinois State Board of Education, the Illinois Association of School Boards, and appropriate educational partners for their consideration and action.

WHEREAS, the Family Justice Resource Center, the ACLU of Illinois, Legal Action Chicago, and the Office of the Cook County Public Defender led a broad coalition of organizations and advocates in advancing the Protecting Innocent Families Act, securing important protections for children and families throughout Illinois; and 

WHEREAS, these four organizations brought complementary expertise, sustained advocacy, and a shared commitment to child safety, family integrity, due process, evidence-based medicine and medical ethics to the advancement of this landmark legislation; and

il-17031-bos-matter-81607.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

HONORING THE PUBLIC SERVICE OF COOK COUNTY COMMISSIONER SEAN M. MORRISON REPRESENTING THE 17TH DISTRICT

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the dedicated public service of Commissioner Sean M. Morrison representing the suburban 17th District, which includes more than 30 municipalities, whose tenure began in July 2015 and will conclude in December 2026; and 

WHEREAS, throughout more than eleven years of service, Commissioner Sean Morrison brought the perspective of a business owner to county government, emphasizing fiscal responsibility, balanced budgets, sound financial management, accountability, and responsible stewardship of taxpayer resources; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison played a leading role in sponsoring the successful repeal of Cook County's Sweetened Beverage Tax in 2017, working across party lines to secure its repeal while supporting the adoption of a subsequent county budget that addressed an approximately $200 million budget shortfall; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison supported stronger pension funding, prudent debt management, and government efficiency, including the consolidation of the Cook County Recorder of Deeds Office into the Cook County Clerk's Office; and

WHEREAS, recognizing the importance of transparency and accountability in public administration, Commissioner Sean Morrison called for greater oversight and Inspector General scrutiny following serious billing and financial-control concerns at Cook County Health; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison consistently supported law enforcement and the resources necessary to protect residents and maintain safe communities, including casting the lone vote in 2020 against a resolution calling for the redirection of funding from policing and incarceration to other services; and

WHEREAS, demonstrating a commitment to addressing the opioid crisis, Commissioner Sean Morrison established an opioid overdose prevention grant program that provided participating police departments with life-saving medication and training to help prevent fatal overdoses with over 200 lives reported saved by police officers; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison worked closely with the Forest Preserves Administration to shepherd the appropriate care, maintenance and growth of our outstanding Forest Preserves for all to enjoy and experience; and

WHEREAS, working in partnership with municipal leaders and county transportation officials, Commissioner Sean Morrison advocated for significant resources in roadway and infrastructure investments throughout the 17th District, supporting improvements that strengthen neighborhoods, promoted economic development, and improved public safety; and
WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison recognized the essential contributions of skilled trades professionals and organized labor in building and maintaining public infrastructure and sustaining the regional economy; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison advocated for property tax relief for senior citizens, greater scrutiny of property classifications, and provided assistance for residents navigating property tax appeals, exemptions, and other county services, while continuing to emphasize the importance of addressing the growing property tax burden on homeowners; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison understood that effective public service requires collaboration and partnership, working alongside mayors, village presidents, municipal managers, township officials, first responders, county employees, fellow commissioners, and community stakeholders to advance the interests of the 17th District; and

WHEREAS, throughout his tenure, Commissioner Sean Morrison remained committed to representing the families, businesses, taxpayers, and communities of the 17th District with dedication, accessibility, and a strong sense of responsibility; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Sean Morrison has represented the 17th District with deep faith, and gratitude for the loving support of his wife Lora and his two daughters; and

WHEREAS, as Commissioner Sean Morrison concludes his service on the Cook County Board at the end of 2026 and returns his full attention to the private sector, his commitment to the communities he has represented will continue; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners believes that dedicated public service deserves recognition and appreciation, particularly when undertaken with a commitment to fiscal responsibility, public safety, infrastructure investment, and accountable government;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners hereby recognize and honor the service, dedication, and accomplishments of Commissioner Sean M. Morrison representing the 17th District from July 2015 to December 2026; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners extends its sincere appreciation for his contributions to the residents, businesses, municipalities, and communities of Cook County, particularly those within the 17th District; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that a suitable copy of this resolution be presented to Commissioner Sean M. Morrison in recognition of his distinguished service and as an expression of the Board's gratitude and best wishes in his future endeavors.

il-17031-bos-matter-81608.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

 HONORING COMMISSIONER DONNA MILLER 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Donna Miller (6th District), has served the residents of the Southland and all of Cook County on the Cook County Board of Commissioners since 2018, bringing to the Board her background in the healthcare industry and an unwavering commitment to health equity; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller is a graduate of Howard University and a former healthcare consultant to leading biotech companies, and has been involved in community, civic and political activities throughout her life, including serving as Board Chair of Planned Parenthood of Illinois and Planned Parenthood of Illinois Action, serving on the Rules Committee at the 2016 Democratic National Convention, and helping bring Cystic Fibrosis into newborn screening in Illinois; and 

WHEREAS, on the Cook County Board, Commissioner Miller served as Chair of Asset Management, Contract Compliance, and Veterans Committees as well as two Forest Preserve District committees, serves as Vice Chair of the Workforce, Housing & Community Development Committee and as a member of the NACo Health Committee and CORE Justice Network, and as a founding board member of the Southland Development Authority; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller has made heart health and lifesaving preparedness a priority, authoring the legislation enabling CPR/AED training for County employees and creating a virtual countywide CPR & AED training program that earned a 2022 National Association of Counties (NACo) Achievement Award; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller sponsored legislation establishing regular Health and Hospitals Committee updates from Cook County Health and the Department of Public Health on Covid-19 and other diseases of concern, as well as semi-annual reviews of health outcome disparities and recommended solutions; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller has been a leading voice on maternal and reproductive health, convening public hearings on maternal morbidity and mortality, sponsoring the legislation declaring it a Public Health Crisis, securing the funding for the first-ever Cook County Health Doula Program, co-sponsoring the women’s reproductive health equity amendment, and carrying these priorities to the national stage through NACo resolutions supporting doula services and uterine fibroid research and by moderating the Black Maternal Health Panels at the NABCO Annual Conferences; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller has championed the safety of women, children and families, sponsoring the Chicago-Cook Violence Against Women Taskforce, hearings on safeguards for domestic violence survivors, and legislation supporting social media safety education and the Kids Online Safety Act; and 
WHEREAS, as the first woman to Chair the Cook County Board Veterans Committee, Commissioner Miller secured additional funding and staffing for the Veterans Assistance Commission of Cook County to increase direct benefits to veterans and their families; and
 
WHEREAS, Commissioner Miller has received numerous honors, including Women of Excellence 2022 from Global Eye Magazine and the Indian American Coalition, Woman of the Year 2023 from the American Multiethnic Coalition, the Advocate for Social Justice Award from Alpha Kappa Alpha Sorority, Incorporated, and a Presidential Lifetime Achievement Award from President Joe Biden for her work in medical equity and awareness; and 

WHEREAS, throughout her years of public service, Commissioner Miller has been dedicated to the needs and values of the residents of Cook County and Illinois, always advocating for accessibility to resources and accountability from government;
  
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby extend our sincere and grateful appreciation to Commissioner Donna Miller for her service on the Cook County Board of Commissioners, particularly her leadership in advancing the health and wellbeing of Cook County residents, and our best wishes to her for continued success, happiness, and good health in the years to come; and

WHEREAS, reaching the remarkable age of 100 is a rare and extraordinary milestone, and Alfredia McDade's life serves as an example of kindness, steadfastness, faith, dedication, and boundless compassion, leaving a lasting legacy for her family and the community she has called home; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the importance of honoring the remarkable individuals whose lives, experiences, and contributions have helped shape our communities, and proudly celebrates Alfredia McDade as a distinguished resident of Cook County whose century of life is worthy of recognition and admiration;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby proudly honor Alfredia M. McDade on the occasion of her 100th birthday, recognizing her extraordinary century of life, her dedication to family and public service, and the lasting impact she has made on those fortunate enough to know and love her; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body and that a suitable copy be presented to Alfredia M. McDade and her family as a lasting symbol of Cook County's respect, admiration, and appreciation on this extraordinary 100th birthday milestone.

WHEREAS, Bridget Gainer was elected to the Cook County Board of Commissioners in 2010 to represent the 10th District, and has served the residents of Cook County with deep affection and gratitude; and

WHEREAS, Cook County gave Commissioner Gainer the opportunity to serve the people of the greatest City in the world; and

WHEREAS, The County Board gave Commissioner Gainer the great privilege to help strengthen the safety net that is Cook County and one that serves all: the sick, the imprisoned, the homeless, the unemployed, the undocumented and does so with a focus on the dignity of the individual not just the service to the system; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Gainer also sought to change that system across many areas, including:

·	Changing HIV testing at Cook County Jail to be dignified and private and immediate, allowing those testing positive to receive treatment; and

·	Reforming the treatment of women and mothers at Cook County Jail, ending the practice of separating new mothers awaiting trial from their newborns and securing passage of legislation prohibiting the shackling of detainees while giving birth; and 

·	Sponsoring concerts and events at the jail for Christmas and Mothers Day bringing countless elected officials responsible for legislating criminal justice into the jail, often for the first time; and
·	Creating the County’s first Pension Committee in 2010, and since serving as its chair where she led a transparent, public effort for a pension reform solution that was fair to both taxpayers and workers; and 

·	Lead the effort to create the Illinois Drivers License for Undocumented people and the County’s sanctuary ordinance; and

·	Lastly, in the wake of the great financial crisis, organized homeowners, advocates, community leaders to create the Cook County Land Bank Authority, established by ordinance in 2013 and since then has chaired its Board, guiding its mission to return vacant land to productive use and to dismantle the delinquent property tax sales that were a vestige of red lining and segregation; and 

WHEREAS, Under her leadership, the Cook County Landbank has created almost 3000 units of housing, built by over 600 neighborhood developers, employing thousands of people and generating over $100MM in property tax revenue, growing the property tax base of Cook County by over $330MM; and 

WHEREAS, The Cook County Landbank serves 76 of the 128 Cook County municipalities and 61 of the 77 Chicago neighborhoods, and has generated over $2 billion in economic impact. 

WHEREAS, through this work, Commissioner Gainer has built partnerships among government, business, and community organizations to improve the lives of Cook County residents and insure that everyone can love where they live; and

WHEREAS, Commissioner Gainer was only able to accomplish these reforms with the partnership of the tremendous men and women who served on the staff with loyalty, intelligence and a commitment to Chicago and Cook County; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Gainer will greatly treasure and equally miss the camaraderie, dedication and fellowship of her fellow Commissioners and forever admire the commitment to justice, dignity and progress of President Preckwinkle and her team; and 

WHEREAS, Commissioner Gainer and was motivated into public service by the example of her parents who were dedicated to their family, their faith, their neighborhood and their City and lived that dedication through action and.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, by the President and Board of Commissioners of the County of Cook, assembled this 19th day of November, 2026, that the Board recognizes and thanks Commissioner Bridget Gainer for her service to the people of Cook County.

il-17031-bos-matter-81619.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

RECOGNIZING NOVEMBER AS NATIONAL VETERANS AND MILITARY FAMILIES’ MONTH

WHEREAS, November is nationally recognized as National Veterans and Military Families’ Month, providing an opportunity to honor the courage, service, and sacrifices of the men and women who have served in the United States Armed Forces, as well as the families who have stood beside them throughout their military service; and

WHEREAS, the history of military service in Cook County is rich and longstanding, with generations of men and women from our communities answering the call to serve in every major conflict in American history, including the Civil War, World Wars I and II, the Korean War, Vietnam War, Desert Storm, the War on Terror, and military operations around the world; and

WHEREAS, Cook County is home to one of the largest veteran populations in the nation, representing approximately one-third of all veterans residing in Illinois, and these veterans have made immeasurable contributions to our nation's security while continuing to strengthen the social, economic, and civic fabric of our communities; and

WHEREAS, Cook County has a longstanding commitment to ensuring veterans and their families receive the services, resources, and recognition they deserve, including through the establishment of the Cook County Veterans Assistance Commission in 1946 and the Cook County Department of Veterans Affairs in 2012, which provide critical assistance with housing, financial support, employment, benefits, and other essential needs; and

WHEREAS, Cook County remains home to vital federal healthcare institutions, including the Edward Hines Jr. Veterans Affairs Hospital and the Jesse Brown Department of Veterans Affairs Medical Center, which provide comprehensive medical care, mental health services, rehabilitation, and specialized treatment to veterans throughout the region; and

WHEREAS, veterans continue to serve their communities long after their military service concludes, bringing leadership, discipline, experience, and dedication to our workforce, public service, local organizations, and neighborhoods throughout Cook County; and

WHEREAS, the sacrifices of military service extend beyond those who wear the uniform, as military families endure deployments, relocations, uncertainty, and the emotional challenges of supporting loved ones in service, demonstrating extraordinary resilience, strength, and commitment; and

WHEREAS, veterans and military families can face unique challenges when transitioning from military to civilian life, including accessing earned benefits, securing affordable housing, finding meaningful employment, obtaining healthcare, and navigating mental health resources, underscoring the importance of continued support and outreach; and

WHEREAS, National Veterans and Military Families’ Month serves as an important reminder that honoring our veterans must extend beyond ceremonies and expressions of gratitude, requiring continued action, investment, and collaboration to ensure those who served our nation and their families have the opportunities and resources they need to thrive; and

WHEREAS, the Cook County Board of Commissioners recognizes the importance of working alongside veteran service organizations, military family support groups, local governments, community partners, and advocates to strengthen services, expand opportunities, and ensure the voices and experiences of veterans and military families remain recognized and valued; and

WHEREAS, as Chair of the Cook County Board of Commissioners' Veterans Committee, Commissioner Donna Miller remains committed to advocating for veterans, recognizing their contributions, and advancing policies and initiatives that improve the quality of life for veterans and their families throughout Cook County;

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the President and Members of the Cook County Board of Commissioners do hereby recognize November as National Veterans and Military Families’ Month in Cook County, honoring the extraordinary service, courage, and sacrifices of our nation's veterans and the families who support them; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Cook County Board of Commissioners encourages all residents, businesses, community organizations, and institutions to recognize and celebrate the contributions of veterans and military families throughout November and to demonstrate their appreciation through meaningful acts of support and service; and

BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that this resolution be spread upon the official proceedings of this Honorable Body as a lasting expression of Cook County's gratitude, respect, and unwavering commitment to the men and women who have served our nation and the families who have served alongside them.

.

il-17031-bos-matter-81623.title:
PROPOSED RESOLUTION

PAULETTE OGBORN, IN MEMORIAM
 
WHEREAS, some lives are measured not simply by the years they encompass, but by the love they inspire, the joy they bring, and the countless hearts they touch along the way. Such was the life of Paulette Ogborn, a remarkable woman whose warmth, grace, vibrant spirit, and devotion to those she loved left an enduring impression upon all who had the privilege of knowing her; and
 
WHEREAS, born on April 19, 1953, in Hillside, Illinois, to the late Paul and Alice Kesmar, Paulette began a life that would take her through Indiana, Arizona, and California before eventually making her home in Tampa, Florida. Wherever life carried her, she brought with her an unmistakable warmth, a love of living, and a gift for making a house feel like home; and
 
WHEREAS, Paulette shared a beautiful and enduring marriage with her beloved husband, Robert Ogborn. Together, they built a life rich in memories, companionship, and devotion, joyfully celebrating their fiftieth wedding anniversary in 2022-a golden milestone honoring half a century of love and a lifetime of shared experiences; and
 
WHEREAS, among Paulette’s greatest joys and proudest accomplishments was being a mother to her three cherished sons, Ethan (Kevin) Ogborn, Jordan (Rebecca) Ogborn, and Aaron Ogborn. To her, motherhood was not merely a responsibility, but a calling she embraced wholeheartedly. She poured her energy, tenderness, creativity, and love into raising her children, creating a home where they could feel safe, valued, and deeply loved; and
 
WHEREAS, Paulette understood that the beauty of a home was never found simply in its furnishings or surroundings, but in the laughter that filled its rooms, the meals lovingly prepared, the traditions shared, and the quiet, everyday acts of kindness that transform ordinary moments into treasured memories; and
 
WHEREAS, Paulette possessed a wonderful enthusiasm for life. She loved cooking, traveling, exercising, exploring the outdoors, and expressing her personality through her impeccable sense of fashion. She appreciated beauty in its many forms and embraced the pleasures of living with a spirit that was both graceful and wonderfully vibrant. Yet among all the things she enjoyed, nothing was more precious to her than the people she loved, especially her children; and
 
WHEREAS, as a devoted wife, mother, daughter, sister, aunt, colleague, and friend, Paulette enriched the lives of those around her through her kindness, generosity of spirit, and sincere affection. She had a special place in her heart for her beloved cats, who knew her tender care, and she possessed that rare and beautiful ability to make others feel welcomed, appreciated, and loved; and
 
WHEREAS, Paulette and her beloved husband, Robert, were active Jehovah’s Witnesses, sharing a faith that was an important and meaningful part of their lives. Their devotion to their congregation and the spiritual values they cherished reflected their desire to live with purpose, compassion, and love for others; and
 
WHEREAS, in 2019, Paulette faced a diagnosis of lymphoma with remarkable courage and perseverance. Although she overcame the lymphoma, she subsequently developed a rare and devastating paraneoplastic syndrome. Throughout the challenges that followed, her life remained a testament to the strength of the human spirit and the profound love that surrounded her; and
 
WHEREAS, on December 3, 2022, Paulette’s earthly life came to a close, leaving behind a family and countless friends who mourn her absence while holding close the extraordinary blessing of having known and loved her; and
 
WHEREAS, although words can never fully capture the beauty of a life or the depth of a family’s loss, Paulette’s legacy lives on in the children she raised, the marriage she nurtured, the friendships she treasured, and the countless memories that continue to bring comfort and smiles to those who knew her; and
 
WHEREAS, Paulette Ogborn deserves to be remembered not only for the roles she fulfilled so faithfully, but for the beautiful, spirited, loving woman she was-a woman who embraced life, delighted in its possibilities, and gave so much of herself to those fortunate enough to share in it; and
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, that the Board of Commissioners of Cook County extends its deepest condolences and heartfelt sympathy to Robert Ogborn, to Paulette’s beloved children and family, and to the many friends whose lives were brightened by her presence; and
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Board joins her loved ones in celebrating the life of Paulette Ogborn, recognizing with gratitude the warmth she shared, the devotion she demonstrated, and the beautiful and lasting legacy of love she leaves behind; and
 
BE IT FINALLY RESOLVED, that this resolution be entered into the official proceedings of the Cook County Board of Commissioners, and that suitable copies be presented to Paulette’s family as an enduring expression of remembrance, respect, and affection.
 
May Paulette Ogborn be remembered not simply for the years of her life, but for the life she brought to those years-and for the love that remains in the hearts of all who knew her.
